title: Set a wheelchair for a pivot transfer: her strong side, 30 to 50 degrees to the bed
instruction: Mrs Hale is sitting on the edge of her bed, about to move to her wheelchair; her left side is weak after a stroke. Set the wheelchair up for a stand-pivot transfer: beside the bed next to her on her strong side (its nearest corner at most 40 mm along the bed past her), within 20 mm of the bed's side (0.4 m and 0.2 m at this 1:10 scale), its front toward the foot of the bed, angled 30 to 50 degrees out from the bed's side, so she can stand, turn on her strong leg and sit down.
context: Nursing assistants, home health aides and personal care aides move residents from bed to wheelchair many times a day. For a resident who can stand but has one weak side, as after a stroke, the usual method is the stand-pivot transfer, and the chair is set up before she stands: beside the bed on her stronger side, right next to her, so that she turns on her strong leg; close to the bed; and angled to it (commonly taught as 30 to 45 degrees; full credit here for 30 to 50), facing the foot of the bed, so that she turns less than a quarter turn before she sits. The common error is the mirror image: the chair parked on her weak side, where she would have to pivot on the weak leg. Brakes and swing-away footrests are part of the real set-up but are not modelled here.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and stands for the floor of a care-home room at 1:10 scale. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Fixed to the table: (1) Bed: a white-painted wooden block 90 mm deep (x 40.0 to 49.0 cm), 240 mm long (y 0 to +24.0 cm) and 48 mm tall; its near side face (x 40.0 cm) faces the arms, its head end is at y +24.0 cm and its foot end at y 0. (2) Pillow: a white-painted wooden block 60 x 40 x 8 mm on the bed at x 41.5-47.5 cm, y 19.5-23.5 cm. (3) Mrs Hale: a rigid seated manikin, one piece of tan plastic (slippers painted dark grey, sling blue cloth), sitting on the bed's near edge facing the arms (facing -x), so her right side is toward +y; her centre line is at y 10.0 cm. Her parts are boxes (x and y in cm, heights above the table in mm): thighs x 39.0-44.5, y 8.0-12.0, 48-63 mm; torso x 43.0-45.5, y 8.0-12.0, 63-113; lower legs x 38.8-40.0, y 8.2-11.8, 0-48 (against the bed's side); dark grey slippers x 36.3-38.8, y 8.2-11.8, 0-8; right arm x 42.5-45.5, y 12.0-12.8, 65-105; left forearm in a blue sling x 41.8-43.0, y 7.4-10.2, 78-92; and the head, a 22 mm sphere centred at x 44.2, y 10.0, 124 mm up. Loose: (4) Wheelchair: one rigid 120 g model (no moving parts) with a 95 x 63 mm footprint, 85 mm tall. Its front is the footplate end; positions below are forward of (+) or behind (-) the middle of its footprint, and heights above the floor. Two rear wheels: dark rubber plates 60 mm long, 2 mm thick and 60 mm tall, one on each side (outer faces 63 mm apart), from -47.5 to +12.5 mm, standing on the floor. Seat: navy vinyl, 50 mm front to back, 59 mm across, 8 mm thick, 42-50 mm up, from -42.5 to +7.5 mm. Backrest: navy, 5 mm thick, 59 mm across, 50-85 mm up, at the back (-47.5 to -42.5 mm). Chromed steel frame: on each side a rail 4 mm wide and 6 mm tall (36-42 mm up, +12.5 to +40 mm) and a front leg 6 x 4 mm (12-42 mm up, +40 to +46 mm); two footplates 16 mm front to back, 22 mm across and 4 mm thick (8-12 mm up, +28 to +44 mm), one either side of the middle line. Two dark rubber castors 10 x 6 x 12 mm tall at the front corners (+37.5 to +47.5 mm). It stands on its wheels and castors with its footprint centre at x 30.0 cm, y -20.0 cm (past the foot of the bed, on her weak side), its front pointing toward the arms and to the left (toward -x and +y, 45 degrees from each). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the wheelchair's pose at the last step, as a top photo with a protractor and a tape would read it. Footprint: the 95 x 63 mm rectangle under its wheels and castors. Angle to the bed (alpha): seen from above, the angle from the bed's side pointing to its foot end (-y) to the chair's front direction, positive turned out toward the room (-x): 0 = parallel to the bed facing its foot, 90 = square to the bed facing the room, negative = turned in toward the bed, over 90 = facing toward the head end. Gap (g): from the bed's near side face (x 40.0 cm) to the footprint's corner nearest it, along x. 'Set down': tilted 10 degrees or less, its lowest point within 3 mm of the table, and still (its footprint centre's path, turns counted at its corners, under 5 mm over the last 0.5 s). Score 0 if it is not set down (tipped, lifted, moving, on the bed or on her); or any footprint corner is at y below 13.0 cm (her strong-side line, just past her right arm: any part on her weak side, in front of her or across her; the start scores 0); or its nearest corner is more than 40 mm along the bed past that line (y over 17.0 cm: too far from her, 0.4 m at scale); or a corner is more than 3 mm past the line of the bed's side face (into the bed); or alpha is below 0 or above 90 degrees; or g is over 80 mm (0.8 m at scale). Otherwise the score is closeness + angle: closeness 0.5 if g is 20 mm or less (0.2 m at scale), else 0; angle 0.5 if alpha is 30 to 50 degrees, 0.25 if 15 to under 30 or over 50 to 65 degrees, else 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Examples, all beside her on her strong side: 10 mm from the bed at 40 degrees 1.0; at 20 or 60 degrees 0.75; parallel (5 degrees) or square (85 degrees) 0.5; 40 degrees but 50 mm off 0.5; 20 degrees and 50 mm off 0.25; parallel and 50 mm off 0. On her weak side, more than 40 mm along the bed past her, turned in or facing the head end: 0 at any distance. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. In a real trial, read alpha with a protractor on a top photo against the bed's side, g with a tape square to it, and the side against lines on the floor at y 13.0 and 17.0 cm.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The bed, pillow and manikin are fixed and she does not move. The wheelchair is one rigid body of twelve boxes: its wheels do not roll (it slides if pushed) and it has no brakes or swing-away footrests, which are not scored. The scorer sees only the chair, so a chair held still within 3 mm of the floor counts as set down.
reset_notes: Stand the wheelchair on its wheels with its footprint centre at x 30.0 cm, y -20.0 cm and its front pointing toward the arms and to the left (toward -x and +y, 45 degrees from each). The bed, pillow and manikin are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
